model_annotation: The image displays two grouped bar charts comparing the percentage values of three metals—Aluminium, Kupfer (Copper), and Nickel—for the years 2021, 2022, and 2023 in two regions: Deutschland (Germany) on the left and the EU on the right. Each chart features a vertical y-axis labeled with percentages (%) ranging from 0 to 30, marked at intervals of 5, and a horizontal x-axis listing the three metal categories. The bars are color-coded: blue for 2021, purple for 2022, and gray for 2023, as indicated by the legend below the charts. In the Deutschland chart, Nickel shows the highest percentages across all years (25.1% in 2021, 24.7% in 2022, and 11.4% in 2023), followed by Kupfer (8.3%, 11.3%, and 2.2%) and Aluminium (3.6%, 2.7%, and 1.0%). In the EU chart, Nickel also has the highest values (24.3% in 2021, 23.3% in 2022, and 14.6% in 2023), followed by Kupfer (4.4%, 5.1%, and 1.3%) and Aluminium (3.2%, 2.8%, and 1.7%). The bars are arranged in groups by metal type, with each group containing three bars representing the respective years. The data for all bars are labeled numerically above each bar, and the bars are ordered from left to right in the sequence Aluminium, Kupfer, Nickel. No visual emphasis such as shading or bolding is applied to any specific bar.
